subject: Service interruption — request for SLA adjudication & telemetry snapshot
messages:
From: Kelsey Moreno <kelsey@blueharbor.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High-rate 503s during checkout — please confirm window & SLA eligibility

Hi Aditya,

We observed a brief but material spike of 503 responses on our checkout path this morning. Impact summary:
- Region: us-west-2
- Window we saw client-side errors: 08:43:12 — 09:02:14 UTC (our logs)
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (tokenization stage) — estimated 12% of checkout attempts failed
- Sample request IDs: bh-req-88ae, bh-req-88b1, bh-req-88c5

This caused order retries and a measurable drop in conversion for ~20 minutes. Can Redwood confirm the server-side availability window and whether this meets the SLA outage definition? We will need the telemetry snapshot (traces, raw request logs) and any preliminary root-cause notes for our procurement team.

Please advise on next steps and what evidence bundle you can share. If this is an SLA-eligible event we will request a credit and a postmortem.

Thanks,
Kelsey Moreno
Sr. DevOps Engineer
BlueHarbor Payments
[Attachment: screenshot-503.png (PNG, 96KB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kelsey Moreno <kelsey@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 09:32:14 -0700
Subject: Re: High-rate 503s during checkout — please confirm window & SLA eligibility

Hi Kelsey — thanks for the flag and the sample IDs. We're opening this on our side now. Quick asks so we can prioritize the evidence pull:
1) Can you confirm whether you saw any client-side retries or circuit-breaker behavior during the window?
2) Do you have the CloudFront request IDs (if available)?
3) Any proxy/logs from your side that show the exact timestamps in UTC (your window helps but I want canonical time alignment).

Immediate next steps from Redwood: Marcus will pull the trace slices and request logs for the time range you specified; we'll validate the exact start/stop timestamps and assess whether the event meets our SLA "service unavailability" criteria (>=X% error rate over a rolling minute threshold).

I'll follow up within 3 business hours with a preliminary window and an evidence bundle link. If this is SLA-eligible, we'll start a remediation/postmortem and estimate a provisional credit amount for your procurement team.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize.

—Aditya Rao
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Internal note: loop in Priyom for telemetry extraction if traces exceed 500MB]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 12:05:48 -0700
Subject: Re: High-rate 503s during checkout — telemetry snapshot ready (prelim)

Aditya/Team — preliminary findings and artifacts attached. Summary:
- Confirmed elevated 503 rate from 08:41:22 UTC through 09:00:55 UTC (internal ingress logs) — matches BlueHarbor’s reported window within clock skew.
- Error profile: majority 503s correlate with a brief autoscaler eviction cycle in us-west-2; we saw repeated worker churn and short-lived allocation failures during the interval.
- Impact magnitude: approx. 10–14% of requests to the /v1/generate service returned 5xx codes, concentrated on mid-length sequences (seq_len 256–512).
- Candidate root cause: autoscaler mis-evaluation during a rolling maintenance job — further verification required from infra team (ticket INF-2029-611).

Attachments included in this thread: redwood_trace_20290605.gz (traces slice, 78MB), request_logs_20290605.json (filtered requests, 24MB). Also linking the internal telemetry snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/DH-8742/2029-06-05

Policy note (for credit eligibility routing): per SLA section 3.2, transient errors caused by autoscaler misconfiguration are generally eligible if they result in sustained error-rate breach for the configured rolling window and affect availability above the floor. Need legal/procurement review for final credit calculation.

Next steps: Priyom — can you extract the KV cache hit rates and batch-sizes for the window and confirm whether prefix caching was disabled during the eviction? Also advise if there's any retention/PII constraints before we share full logs with BlueHarbor.

—Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_trace_20290605.gz (GZIP, 78MB); Attachment: request_logs_20290605.json (JSON, 24MB)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kelsey Moreno <kelsey@blueharbor.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Jun 2029 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service interruption — request for SLA adjudication & telemetry snapshot

Kelsey — following up with formal next steps and what we can share. Thank you again for the detailed report. Summary of actions and timeline:

1) Confirmed server-side window: 2029-06-05T08:41:22Z — 2029-06-05T09:00:55Z (Redwood ingress logs). This aligns within clock skew to the timeframe you provided.

2) Evidence bundle shared: traces + filtered request logs + screenshot. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-example-evidence (access granted to your ops group).

3) Preliminary eligibility: based on our assessment, this appears to meet the availability breach threshold under Section 3.2 of the SLA (error-rate sustained breach due to autoscaler churn). We're routing this to billing for a provisional credit calculation and to Legal for contract-level review.

4) Postmortem plan & timeline: Redwood will produce a public postmortem with a technical RCA and remediation steps within 7 business days. We will include: root cause, corrective actions (autoscaler tuning + canary release safeguards), and a follow-up verification window.

5) Data handling & redaction: Priyom — please confirm by EOD Monday that the supplied logs have no customer PII and that the KV-key traces are redacted as needed.

Please let me know if BlueHarbor needs a formal credits request form (we can push a prefilled DocuSign). Otherwise we’ll proceed with the internal adjudication and circle back with a provisional credit number by Tue COB.

Apologies again for the impact — we’ll prioritize the RCA and mitigation.

—Aditya Rao
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Forwarded attachments: redwood_trace_20290605.gz; request_logs_20290605.json; screenshot-503.png]
